title: I Became We by Mona Pirnot and Jack D. Coen at Atlantic Theater Compa...
transcript: I've seen hundreds of theatrical productions, so it's rare for me to consider something truly innovative. Mona Pirnot is 3 for 3 in creating cool, weird, and innovative work with her most recent world premieres. Her latest, I Became We, is essentially an autobiographical solo monologue delivered as a choral piece by an ensemble of 16. It unfolds like a journal entry with humorous candor and confessional reflections. The degree of intimacy feels magnified by the fact that it's performed by a choir, in that it strips away a layer of theatrical characterization in favor of just delivering the text. Of course, musicalizing it still heightens the material, and this composition by Jack D. Coen is rich and expressive. Stylistically, it's at times jovial, at other times lush and sumptuous, cultivating a wide but distinct soundscape in just 70 minutes. In the world of classical music, English is considered a clunky and difficult language to sing in, so it's impressive and kind of funny to hear modern English sung in such a formal style. This piece really leans into that humor, brilliantly executing a brilliant concept. I also appreciate Atlantic Theater Company being willing to go out on a limb and produce something so unorthodox, and hopefully other companies are picking up on Mona Pirnot's genius. I already can't wait for her next piece, but for now, make sure you catch this one.
